messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — customer 'ClearView' on Dedicated is reporting repeated 429s during their morning ramp. They say the service didn't scale for ~3m despite traffic spike. stack traces show API 429s not 503s.

rachel: thx. do we have any telemetry? which cluster/region?

sanjay: region-us-west2, dedicated pool 'cv-usw2-pool-1'. I pulled recent autoscaler logs, see a sequence:
```
[03:20:01] probe: observed qps spike -> trigger scale request (desired=12)
[03:20:02] allocator: allocation in-progress -> enqueue request id=abc123
[03:20:30] warmchain: minReplicas=8, maxReplicas=20
[03:21:30] provider: imagepull backoff on nodes x,y -> retries
[03:22:45] autoscaler: scale stuck at 8 due to attach-timeout -> fallback to probe-only
```

rachel: hmm imagepull/backoff + attach-timeout is classic coldstart compounding. are these pods stuck in Pending or CrashLoop?

jen_ops: i checked kube: many stay Pending with reason=ImagePullBackOff and some Pending due to InsufficientCPU. Also saw the warm-pool heartbeat delayed (heartbeats from warmpool-hosts were 30s late).

eli_ml: curious if this is noisy neighbor on the same nodegroup — could be spike in image pulls saturating registry throughput. any recent deployments around that time?

sanjay: customer said they did a deploy ~03:18 which bumped concurrent model sizes (larger images). Also our registry throttling alert fired around 03:19.

oncall-bot: :warning: alert registry.rate_limit_triggered - cv-usw2-pool-1 - count=4 in 5m

rachel: that aligns. two factors: larger images (slower pulls) + registry rate limits -> attach latency -> autoscaler doesn't reach desired before customer QPS hits concurrency gate.

jen_ops: quick repro commands I ran:
```bash
# simulate spike and large image pulls
kubectl create -f heavy-deploy.yaml --replicas=16
watch kubectl get pods -o wide --namespace=dedicated-cv
```
Observed controller stuck at 8 for ~2:40.

eli_ml: mitigation suggestions: 1) increase minReplicas temporarily to 12 for this customer, 2) enable image pre-pull on warm-pool instances, 3) relax probe/concurrency gate thresholds for short window, 4) request registry rate limit bump for their account.

sanjay: customer asks for immediate mitigation — they want guaranteed headroom. Can we do a one-off reserve?

rachel: we can modify their Dedicated config to set minReplicas=12 and set a burst reserve of ephemeral capacity if available. tagging @jen_ops to run change and @eli_ml to double-check costs/SLAs.

jen_ops: starting change now:
```json
{"action":"patch","target":"cv-usw2-pool-1","minReplicas":12}
```
I'll monitor provisioning and share logs.

oncall-bot: :information_source: change requested by rachel applied to queue (change-id=chg-9072).

jen_ops: after patch, new pods began pulling images; registry still throttling but with more parallel pulls we hit ready=11 at 03:25:10, traffic 429s dropped. full recovery ~03:26.

eli_ml: follow-ups: we should add a pre-pull option for large images, add an autoscaler backoff metric to detect attach-timeouts earlier, and consider a per-customer warmpool size param (to avoid noisy neighbor impact).

sanjay: customer notified and less upset now. they're asking for a permanent solution (want guaranteed headroom during morning ramp).

rachel: action items summarized: [jen_ops] make per-customer minReplicas/burst config editable via Console (short-term patch), [eng-runtime] work with infra to add pre-pull and attach-timeout metric, [support] draft runbook for customers to size images and schedule deploys outside ramps.

eli_ml: I'll open an eng ticket (ENG-RND-960) for warm-pool pre-pull + autoscaler metric. tagging eng-runtime leads.

jen_ops: note — this was not an auth/billing issue. registry throttling + large image pulls + minreplica floor = compound coldstart. adding to postmortem folder.

rachel: thanks team. if anything else pops up I'll ping. :thumbsup:
